details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1863-1865, 2083-2097, 2234 (also 619) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: On the "fix-up closed without merging" path, the wait comment is patched to `done` at line 2083 before the no-wait close at line 2234 runs. On every later run, line 1865 sets `wait_ended_at` to the patch time, so the `$block.at > $after` guard rejects the block. A failed or skipped close is therefore never retried.
  WHY: Example: fix-up #50 closed at 09:30Z, block at 10:00Z, judge run at 12:00Z. A `comment_failed`, `label_failed` or `close_failed` close, or an early return before line 2234 (lines 2174/2212/2220/2226), sends the next run to the model verdict and CRITICAL escalation (the #9215 pattern). A `close_failed` close also leaves the issue open with `ai:closed` and a close comment already posted. This breaks the #8470 retry invariant. Both reviewers rated it MAJOR, mapped here to high.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:2083-2085, 2091-2097, 2234-2235 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: When a fix-up closes without merging and a qualifying block came after its `closed_at`, the run patches the wait comment and then runs the close path (comment, `ai:closed` label, close). That is four writes in one run.
  WHY: This goes over the issue's three-write limit and contradicts the claim in agents.d/9518-unblock-nothing-to-implement-no-wait.md:2 that there is no wait-comment update. The source rated it NIT, mapped here to low.
- agents.d/9518-unblock-nothing-to-implement-no-wait.md:2 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The fragment says "No reads, at most the same three writes (comment, label, close), and no wait-comment update." The closed-without-merging path actually patches the wait comment (scripts/unblock_judge.sh:2083) before the three close writes, which makes four writes.
  WHY: This is a documentation defect. Once folded into agents.md it becomes the contract for this path, so anyone sizing the API budget from it will undercount, and it is inconsistent with the #8470 entry (agents.md:5351). All three reviewers rated it NIT, mapped here to low.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:2083-2085 vs 626 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: On the closed-without-merging path, the same item gets two contradictory comments. The wait comment says "Fix-up #50 did not merge in time; the unblock judge decides again." The close comment says "…and no fix-up is pending."
  WHY: Operators and the workflow log analysis see a `fixup=50 done` "decides again" marker next to a completed close that says nothing was pending, and the wait text is the one that is wrong. The source rated it NIT, mapped here to low.
- changelog.d/unblock-nothing-to-implement-no-wait.md:6 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The changelog gives the wait-end time as "this run when the judge times it out". It leaves out that `fixup_closed_at` is used when the fix-up closes without merging (scripts/unblock_judge.sh lines 2095-2097).
  WHY: A closure is not a timeout, so the wording can mislead readers about the wait-end comparison. The source rated it NIT, mapped here to low.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: The fragment and changelog should accurately document the API cost and the wait-end condition, including the newly added "closed without merging" path.
  expected_change_site: agents.d/9518-unblock-nothing-to-implement-no-wait.md and changelog.d/unblock-nothing-to-implement-no-wait.md
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: The documents still claim "no wait-comment update" and use simplified "timeout" wording that does not cover the `closed_at` logic in the final script.
- requirement: "§15: reuse the item comments the judge already reads (`${RUNTIME_DIR}/item_comments.json`). No new reads; at most the existing three writes." (linked issue #9518, Constraints)
  expected_change_site: scripts/unblock_judge.sh — the #9518 close call site (line 2234) and the fix-up-closed branch it is reached from (lines 2083-2097)
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: `unblock_patch_comment "${wait_id}" "… did not merge in time; the unblock judge decides again. … done -->"` at scripts/unblock_judge.sh:2083 runs before the three close writes at lines 634-647, so that path makes four writes. No hunk keeps that path to three writes, and agents.d/9518-unblock-nothing-to-implement-no-wait.md:2 documents the opposite.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:unblock_main lines 2083-2097 (the wait comment is marked done, then `wait_ended_at="${fixup_closed_at}"`), the call at line 2234 (`unblock_nothing_to_implement_close "" "" "${tracking}" "${wait:+${wait_ended_at:-${wait_updated:-}}}"`), and the done branch at lines 1863-1865 (`wait_ended_at="${wait_updated}"`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The wait comment is rewritten with the `done` marker at line 2083 before the close is tried at line 2234. On later runs, unblock_latest_wait (line 228) reports `done` with updated set to the rewrite time, and line 1865 uses that time, so `($after == "" or $block.at > $after)` fails and the close is never retried.
  WHY: Example: fix-up #50 closed `not_planned` at 09:30Z, block at 10:00Z, run at 12:00Z. A `comment_failed`, `label_failed` or `close_failed` close returns 0 and promises a retry. The next run sees 10:00Z ≤ 12:00Z, so the issue goes to the model verdict and CRITICAL escalation (the #9215 pattern). `close_failed` also leaves the issue open with `ai:closed` and a close comment. The same loss happens when an earlier exit returns 0 before line 2234 (lines 2174, 2212, 2220, 2226). The #8470 path marks the wait done only after the close succeeds (lines 2038-2043). The test `test_nothing_to_implement_closes_after_a_fixup_closed_without_merging` covers only a single successful run. Suggested fix: keep the end time in a form that survives the rewrite (for example `ended=<ts>` in the done marker, read back near line 1865), and add a test that re-runs a `close_failed` case against the done wait.
- HARDENING (scripts/unblock_judge.sh, unblock_main lines 2083-2097): write `fixup_closed_at` into the done wait comment body and read it back on the done branch near line 1865, falling back to `wait_updated`. Estimated 8-10 lines changed. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3.
- No task gaps reported. The reviewer judged that minimax's pass-1 "three writes" point holds only in a narrow sense and did not raise it as a separate finding.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- agents.d/9518-unblock-nothing-to-implement-no-wait.md:2 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The fragment incorrectly states that the no-wait close makes "at most the same three writes (comment, label, close), and no wait-comment update."
  WHY: The closed-without-merging path runs `unblock_patch_comment` on the wait comment before the new close, which makes four writes. This misleads operators about API cost and is inconsistent with the #8470 entry.
- changelog.d/unblock-nothing-to-implement-no-wait.md:6 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The description of the wait-end comparison is slightly inaccurate for the "closed without merging" path.
  WHY: It says "or this run when the judge times it out", but the code also uses `fixup_closed_at` when the fix-up closes without merging (lines 2095-2097 of `scripts/unblock_judge.sh`). That is a closure, not a timeout.
- TASK_GAP | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  Requirement: The fragment in `agents.d/9518-unblock-nothing-to-implement-no-wait.md` and `changelog.d/unblock-nothing-to-implement-no-wait.md` should accurately document the API cost and the wait-end condition, including the newly added "closed without merging" path.
  Expected change site: agents.d/9518-unblock-nothing-to-implement-no-wait.md and changelog.d/unblock-nothing-to-implement-no-wait.md
  Evidence of absence: The documents still claim "no wait-comment update" and use simplified "timeout" terminology that does not fully cover the `closed_at` logic in the final script.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:2083-2097 (wait-comment patch + `wait_ended_at` derivation), 2234 (the #9518 close call site), 1863-1865 (the `done`-wait branch), 619 (the `$after` guard in the close's jq) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The wait is patched to `done` at line 2083 before the close decision. On the next run, line 1865 sets `wait_ended_at` to the patch time and the `else` branch at line 1867 (which reads `closed_at`) is skipped, so the guard `$block.at > $after` (line 619) rejects the block and a failed close write is never retried.
  WHY: Example: fix-up #50 closed at 09:30Z, block at 10:00Z, run at 12:00Z, and the label POST or close PATCH fails (`outcome=skip reason=label_failed|close_failed`). The next run checks 10:00Z > 12:00Z, which is false, so the item falls through to the model verdict (the #9215 symptom). This breaks the #8470 retry invariant (agents.md:5351).
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:2083-2085 (wait comment text) vs 626 (close comment text) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The wait comment says "Fix-up #50 did not merge in time; the unblock judge decides again." while the close comment says "…and no fix-up is pending."
  WHY: Operators and log analysis see contradictory comments: a `<!-- ai:unblock-wait:v1 item=7 fixup=50 done -->` "decides again" marker next to a completed close that says nothing was pending.
- agents.d/9518-unblock-nothing-to-implement-no-wait.md:line 2 — "No reads, at most the same three writes (comment, label, close), and no wait-comment update." | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The fragment declares three writes and no wait-comment update. The path makes four writes, because the wait patch at scripts/unblock_judge.sh:2083 runs before the close writes at 634-647. This conflicts with the #8470 entry at agents.md:5351.
  WHY: The fragment becomes the agents.md contract and understates the API budget. The kill switch `UNBLOCK_NOTHING_TO_IMPLEMENT_CLOSE_ENABLED` is unaffected (.github/workflows/unblock_judge.yml:178), so this is a declaration gap only.

  Requirement: "§15: reuse the item comments the judge already reads (`${RUNTIME_DIR}/item_comments.json`). No new reads; at most the existing three writes." (linked issue #9518, Constraints)
  Expected change site: scripts/unblock_judge.sh — the #9518 close call site (line 2234) and the fix-up-closed branch it is reached from (lines 2083-2097)
  Evidence of absence: The wait patch at scripts/unblock_judge.sh:2083 runs before the three close writes at lines 634-647, which makes four writes. No hunk keeps that path to three writes, and agents.d/9518-unblock-nothing-to-implement-no-wait.md:2 documents the opposite.
